subject: Ground Works, hidden labour and a possible HKU PhD enquiry
body:
Dear Professor Seng,

Your [HKU research profile](https://www.arch.hku.hk/staff/arch/seng-eunice-m-f/) connects housing, labour and public space; the Anthology programme also pairs you with Replicable Systems.

Resistant City and your published housing, labour and public-space research suggest a way to keep Proxy Society's AI question architectural. I propose following one library or community-centre arrival task: who grants access, whose presence is recognised, and which staff work disappears from the plan when an agent acts for a visitor. Drawings and film would compare ordinary booking, human help and staged delegation.

Would you be open to a short discussion about the historical and observational method, and whether this could fit an HKU architecture PhD with appropriate supervision? I can send a focused two-page proposal.

Best wishes,
Kris Haamer

Would you critique the handoff scenario and the way the plan allocates discretion between visitor, staff and operator?

The [published 2026 Anthology programme](https://www.anthologyfest.com/_files/ugd/888feb_27950b80f5634c118b2d2a23148f27cb.pdf) lists you as a named participant for “Care Beyond the Building”. That is the published connection behind this enquiry.

I would draw how two people approach, wait and cross paths around an AI-assisted community-building entrance, then test whether a clearer transaction route accidentally reduces occasions to meet. Tetawowe's published narrative approach and your Collective Presence pairing make that small spatial consequence a useful subject for critique.

Could you and Tey Tat Sing advise which everyday interactions should be recorded, and whether a studio plan could serve as a published comparison?

Best wishes,
Kris Haamer
Proxy Society
